subject: works fine on Mac, crashes on Linux cluster.

messages.author: 188806804221876c
messages.subject: works fine on Mac, crashes on Linux cluster.
parts:
Dear All, 

my code compiles and works fine on Mac.

On a Linux cluster I get a lot of warning messages at compile time.
They are reported below.

When I run on the linux cluster, stan dies (in most of the attempts) claiming a compilation error.

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 

  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! g++: Internal error: Killed (program cc1plus)



I wonder whether you have an idea about what is going wrong on the cluster (I re-installed rstan and Rcpp).

Compile time messages:

--- Linking C++ model ---

g++ -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -I src -I stan_2.8.0/src -isystem stan_2.8.0/lib/stan_math_2.8.0/ -isystem stan_2.8.0/lib/stan_math_2.8.0/lib/eigen_3.2.4 -isystem stan_2.8.0/lib/stan_math_2.8.0/lib/boost_1.58.0 -Wall -pipe -DEIGEN_NO_DEBUG  -lpthread  -O3 -o hierarchical/hierarchical-t-test src/cmdstan/main.cpp -include hierarchical/hierarchical-t-test.hpp

messages.subject: Re: works fine on Mac, crashes on Linux cluster.
parts:
On Friday, April 22, 2016 at 5:17:39 AM UTC-4, Gcorani wrote:
When I run on the linux cluster, stan dies (in most of the attempts) claiming a compilation error.

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 

  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! g++: Internal error: Killed (program cc1plus)

That is usually because it runs out of RAM. If there is nothing that can be done about that, you can try clang++ instead of g++. In any event, you should try with a more recent version of Stan.

Ben
